decision_maker: Assets & Community Safety Portfolio Holder, Partnerships Portfolio Holder
content:
To formally approve
that Tendring District Council signs-up to the Women’s Safety
Charter.

The Tendring
District Women’s Safety Charter is a preventative, community
safety initiative designed to improve how safe women and girls feel
in public spaces.
 
Safety Charters
have been introduced in several areas of the UK since 2021, many
with an initial focus on the night-time economy. Tendring’s
Charter takes a broader approach by recognising the needs of women
and girls living, working and travelling in more rural
communities.
 
For the year ending
December 2025, 3,529 VAWG offences were recorded by police in
Tendring District. Of these, 328 occurred in public spaces. Police
data shows a reduction in these offences over the previous 12
months; however, recorded crime only reflects incidents reported to
the police.
 
In 2024/25,
Tendring District recorded 4,931 VAWG offences, including domestic
abuse. It is also recognised that police-recorded data does not
capture the full prevalence of violence against women and girls, as
these offences are significantly underreported across the UK.
 
A Women’s
Safety Charter depends on collaboration and commitment from a wide
range of partners. Its aims must be shared across the District and
delivered in partnership with local community groups, policing
teams, education providers, leisure facilities, retail settings and
other relevant organisations.

Taking no action to
roll out the Women’s Safety Charter would mean that the
Council and the Community Safety Partnership do not support the
Government’s plan to tackle violence against women and girls,
or the priorities of both the Council and the Community Safety
Partnership. Not supporting this work would therefore be
inconsistent with the current priorities of both the Council and
the Community Safety Partnership.

purpose:
To seek the agreement of Cabinet to endorse
the renewal of the Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) in Clacton
town centre and its peripheral areas which expires August
2026.
content:
To extend the
Public Spaces Protection Order for Clacton Town Centre for a period
of three years until September 1st, 2029, which will see
this order through Local Government Reorganisation.

To enable the
Portfolio Holder for Assets and Community Safety to consider the
renewal.
 
There has been a
Public Spaces Protection Notice since 2007 in Clacton Town Centre
and then in 2023 for Clacton Town Centre and surrounding Areas.
 
This enables Essex
Police and Tendring District Council Enforcement team and the
Community Safety Accredited Officers to remove alcohol from street
drinkers, disperse groups and tackle Anti-Social Behaviour.
 
The Anti-Social
Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 enacted powers to create
Public Spaces Protection Orders (PSPO). 
The purpose of a PSPO is to stop individuals or groups committing
anti-social behaviour in a public space.

The aim is to
improve areas in Tendring that have been subjected to Anti-Social
behaviour where street drinkers and people congregate and where
criminal activity takes place.
 
Essex Police rely
on the PSPO to respond to Anti-Social Behaviour in the Town
Centre.
 
To not support this
work would be out of line with the Council’s Crime Reduction
and Disorder Strategy and the Community Safety Partnership
Priorities.
 
Essex Police have
confirmed that they use the PSPO on a daily
basis in Clacton Town Centre. This ensures enforcement
activities can take place, alongside crime prevention. The PSPO
provides a tool to ensure the swift resolution of Anti-Social
Behaviour. If the extension is not agreed, it would also impact on
tourism with reduced powers to tackle street drinking and would
potentially see a rise in Anti-Social Behaviour.

To enter into a
consultancy agreement with Local Government East, at an estimated
project value of £96,050, for specialist asset management
support delivered through Local Government East’s Talent
Bank.

The Council
requires additional specialist capacity to progress asset
management and Community Asset Transfer work alongside existing
service demands and LGR preparation. Commissioning this support
will help reduce the risk of delay or incomplete transition
planning.

The alternatives
considered were to seek support from a private sector provider,
resource the work in-house, or defer the appointment. A private
sector appointment would require additional procurement activity
and may not provide the same level of local government knowledge or
value for money. Resourcing the work in-house is not considered
feasible given current capacity and wider LGR demands.
 
Deferral is not
recommended because the work is required now to support LGR
preparation and transition planning.
 
Commissioning
through Local Government East is considered the most proportionate
option, securing specialist expertise within the recorded officer
decision-making framework, Cabinet’s aforementioned funding delegation and the
public-to-public/Teckal procurement
exemption route available through the Talent Bank.

content:
To approve the
additional fee of £4,500 for the roof repairs to the roof
ridge damages at Sunspot with CAMCLAD CONTRACTORS Ltd. for
the Ten_04 Sunspot Solar Panels project, which is being delivered
as part of the Community Regeneration Partnership funding
programme, to upgrade the solar panels at Sunspot to 58kwh.

Damage to the roof
ridge was identified which requires repair before the solar panel
installation can be completed safely and effectively. The proposed
roof repairs are necessary to:
 

Protect the
integrity of the building structure.
Ensure the safe
installation and operation of the solar photovoltaic system.
Prevent delays to
the delivery of the project.
Support the
successful completion of the Community Regeneration Partnership
funded programme.

 
The additional cost
of £4,500 can be met from the contingency provision
already allocated within the Community Regeneration Partnership
Ten_04 Sunspot Solar Panels project budget and therefore does not
require additional funding.
 
To achieve this,
the contractor has submitted a proposal to repair the roof setting
out proposed detail to rectify the issue and avoid a recurrence,
including guarantees offered.

Option 1: Do not undertake
the roof repairs.

This option was rejected as it could compromise the integrity of
the roof, result in delays to the solar panel installation, and
potentially increase future maintenance costs.
 
Option 2: Procure an
alternative contractor.

This option was rejected as CAMCLAD Contractors Ltd is already
mobilised on site and best placed to undertake the necessary
repairs efficiently and with minimal disruption to the project
programme. Camclad were the original
roof installer and as such are familiar with both working
environment and roof build-up. They have confirmed they will honour
the collateral warranty in place for the existing construction and
provide updated as built information.

content:
To submit an
Expression of Interest to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and
Local Government (MHCLG) for Playground Fund grant funding to
support the creation, improvement or enhancement of playground
provision within the District.

The MHCLG
Playground Fund is intended to improve children and young
people’s access to high-quality, accessible and inclusive
play spaces, particularly in areas of greatest need. Submitting an
Expression of Interest will enable the Council to be considered for
external grant funding to support improvements to existing
playgrounds and/or the creation of enhanced play provision. The
funding opportunity aligns with the Council’s priorities for
supporting healthy, active and inclusive communities, improving
public realm assets, and targeting investment where it can deliver
clear community benefit. Submission of the Expression of Interest
does not commit the Council to expenditure beyond the requirements
of the funding process, and any subsequent acceptance of grant will
be subject to the Council’s usual governance, financial and
procurement requirements.

Not to submit an
Expression of Interest.
 
This option was
rejected as it would prevent the Council from being considered for
external funding that could support improvements to playground
provision and deliver benefits for children, families and local
communities. The submission of an Expression of Interest is
considered a proportionate step, as it enables the Council to
explore the opportunity without committing to delivery expenditure
unless funding is confirmed and appropriate approvals are in
place.

purpose:
The Council is currently progressing the
review of its Local Plan and is expected to carry out the final
stage of public consultation during Autumn 2026. The Council also
conducts public consultation exercises on other Planning Policy
documents and therefore requires a robust and reliable online
consultation platform to receive, manage and analyse
representations from residents, statutory consultees and other
stakeholders.
The Council has used the JDi Solutions OpusConsult system since
2023. The system has operated effectively over the past three years
and continues to meet the Council’s operational requirements.
Retention of the platform will support the efficient delivery of
statutory planning consultations and provide a stable solution
throughout the transition to Local Government Reorganisation.

The following benefits will be realised:
1)Continuity - The existing system fulfils all requirements of the
Planning Policy consultation process. As the Council is at a
critical stage of the Local Plan Review, changing systems at this
time would be disruptive, requiring officer training, system
familiarisation and the migration of existing consultation
data.
2)Compliance with data security and accessibility standards. JDi
Solutions complies with relevant cyber security, data protection
and accessibility standards. An initial Data Protection Risk
Assessment was completed when the system was first procured, and
the system was considered low risk. The software incorporates a
number of GDPR safeguards which help minimise the risk of human
error when processing personal data.
3)Value for Money. The costs quoted by JDi Solutions are lower than
those of other comparable systems available through the G-Cloud 14
Framework and avoid the additional implementation, training and
migration costs associated with changing supplier.
4)Customer Service. Council officers have worked directly with JDi
Solutions since 2023 and have found the company’s support
service to be responsive, reliable and flexible in meeting
operational requirements.
5)Compliant procurement route. The proposed direct award is being
undertaken through the Crown Commercial Services G-Cloud 14
Framework in accordance with the Council’s procurement rules
of procedure.
6)Existing budget provision. The contract can be funded from
existing Planning budgets and does not require additional financial
provision.

Strategies Report for the Carnarvon Road car park temporary closure
is six weeks. It needs to be completed to:
- inform a decision by October on when to start demolition of the
existing car park within the CAT Contractor’s programme as
provided in their recent tender submission; and
- Include the peak need for parking in Clacton over the summer
season which has already begun.
- The results of this study will allow mitigation measures to be
implemented in a timely fashion, allowing demolition works to take
place within the programme.
We note that the full scope proposed for this consultancy included
a broader study, in partnership with Pride in Place’s Parking
and Movement Study. However, this decision is to allow for the
immediately required component of the study only related to
mitigations for the closure of the Carnarvon Terrace Carpark.
Quotes have been requested to three consultants but only one has
provided a quote.
The value for money assessment of the fee proposal was constrained
by the limited level of market testing achieved through the
procurement process, as only one compliant quotation was received.
This was a key factor in the decision to reduce the scope of works
to the minimum required to deliver the immediate elements of the
study.
However, while there are no directly comparable quotations for the
reduced scope proposed within this commission, the methodologies
required to undertake the study are well established and industry
standard. On this basis, the proposed fee appears proportionate
when compared with similar parking studies commissioned elsewhere.
Relevant benchmark examples include:
• Parking Survey, Dovercourt Town Centre and Harwich (Tendring
District Council, 2024): Alpha Parking submitted a fee proposal of
£13,420 for a two-day survey programme similar to that
proposed for this study. However, the commission covered a
significantly smaller number of on-street and off-street parking
locations and included a more limited scope for improvement
recommendations.
• Parking Review, Bognor Regis, Littlehampton and Arundel:
Markides successful bid included a fee proposal of £35,000
for a comprehensive review of the parking estate across two seaside
resorts and a historic market town, including beat surveys and
assessment of seasonal demand variations. The study ultimately
demonstrated the continued need for the Bognor Regis multi-storey
car park to accommodate peak seasonal demand.
In addition, Markides is a recognised specialist consultancy with
significant experience in parking and transport studies. Given the
importance of undertaking the surveys during the current summer
season, it was concluded that the programme and delivery risks
associated with re-tendering would outweigh the relatively low risk
of proceeding with the appointment in the absence of further
directly comparable quotations. Accordingly, the proposal is
considered to represent an acceptable balance of value for money,
service quality and timely project delivery.
The additional elements included within the original scope may be
procured separately, subject to the normal approvals route for the
Pride in Place programme, supported by a more detailed
specification and an increased quality weighting. It is anticipated
that this approach will attract a greater number of submissions,
enabling a more robust assessment of both price and the quality and
reliability of the proposed methodologies.

engineering design during the PCSA stage. Ermine's structural

approximately 30m depth to provide sufficient ground data to inform
foundation design and reduce construction risk.
Whilst intrusive ground investigations have already been completed
at the site, the previous borehole did not achieve the depth
required by the contractor's design team. Soiltechnics Ltd have

using a larger rig capable of achieving the required depth.

robust contract sum for the main construction works. The quotation
has been reviewed by Baily Garner LLP, who have confirmed the rates
are reasonable and representative of current market costs.

content:
To approve the
utilisation of £75,000 held within the Brook Park West
commuted sum reserve to support the Council's maintenance
obligations associated with the site, specifically:
 

1.  
The release of £25,000 during 2026/27 to fund the
purchase of a cut and collect ride-on mower required to maintain
Brook Park West in accordance with the approved Landscape
Management and Maintenance Plan.

2.  
The retention of the remaining £50,000 within the
reserve and its phased release into the Open Spaces revenue budget
over years 2–10 to support ongoing maintenance and
operational costs associated with the site.
 
The equipment will
be procured in accordance with the Council's Procurement Procedure
Rules and Financial Procedure Rules.

During 2024/25, the
Council received a commuted sum of £75,000 in respect of the
future maintenance of Brook Park West, Clacton-on-Sea.
 
The approved
Landscape Management and Maintenance Plan require amenity grass
areas to be cut regularly throughout the growing season, with grass
arisings collected and removed from site. The Open Spaces Service
is now responsible for maintaining these areas and requires
appropriate equipment to deliver the required maintenance standards
efficiently and effectively.
 
The purchase of a
dedicated cut and collect ride-on mower will enable the Council to
fulfil its maintenance obligations, reduce reliance on external
contractors, improve service efficiency and ensure compliance with
the approved management plan. The phased release of the remaining
commuted sum will provide an ongoing revenue contribution towards
future maintenance costs and help ensure the long-term
sustainability of the site.
 
The proposal
represents the most effective use of the commuted sum and ensures
that the funding is utilised for the purpose for which it was
originally provided.

Option 1 –
Continue using existing equipment
 
Rejected as
existing machinery does not provide the capability to collect and
remove grass arisings efficiently, which is a requirement of the
approved maintenance plan.
 
Option 2 –
Employ external contractors to undertake the work
 
Rejected as this
would result in higher long-term costs and reduce operational
flexibility.
 
Option 3 –
Retain the entire commuted sum within reserves
 
Rejected as this
would not provide the equipment required to meet the site's
immediate maintenance obligations and would delay delivery of the
maintenance standards expected.
topline: The Open Space, Bereavement & Transport Manager has decided to approve the use of £75,000 for the purchase of maintenance equipment at Brook Park West.

purpose:
The Council’s current arrangement with
iHasco for the delivery of e-learning is due to end on 27 July
2026. A due diligence exercise has been undertaken to consider the
Council’s current usage, the proposed cost of a new one-year
agreement, and indicative comparator costs from alternative
providers.
The assessment demonstrates that iHasco provides the most
cost-effective option when considered against usage levels, course
breadth, service continuity and the Council’s need to
maintain access to mandatory and operational training. A reduced
annual fee has also been negotiated, providing further assurance
that the proposed new agreement represents value for money.
A new one-year agreement provides continuity of training provision
while maintaining flexibility in the context of Local Government
Reorganisation (LGR). A longer agreement period was considered;
however, this was not considered appropriate at this stage, as it
would reduce the Council’s ability to review future learning
and development requirements as part of wider LGR planning. The
one-year agreement also preserves the option of exploring
collaborative procurement arrangements with partner authorities in
the future, should this be considered beneficial.

decision_maker: Corporate Director (Place & Wellbeing) & Deputy Chief Executive
purpose:
Regeneration in Clacton-on-Sea
The Carnarvon Terrace scheme is the most significant TDC-led scheme
within wider regeneration investment across Clacton-on-Sea,
supported by the Local Regeneration Fund, Pride in Place and
Community Regeneration Partnership. Together, the programmes are
working to deliver greater social wellbeing for residents, a
healthier and more sustainable economy, with an enhanced and more
diverse town centre offer, driving growth within Clacton to
catalyse private sector investment.
In Clacton-on-Sea, working alongside Essex County Council,
Carnarvon Road will see £30.35m investment transforming the
existing library and town centre car park into a new Civic Quarter,
with:
•new affordable homes will be provided on a currently derelict
site in a sought-after location in Tendring;
•the existing 300-space car parking provision rationalised
into a modern multi storey structure, opening up this key site for
improved landscaping and public spaces and commercial spaces for
civic use. Provisions of electric charging spaces will future proof
residents' transport offer while meeting needs of residents;
•a community hub including a new library, adult community
learning space for upskilling residents and space for public sector
partners, community space for upskilling residents, and commercial
space for public sector partners in a convenient location.
Progress update
A summary of progress made to date, including design, planning and
procurement milestones and recent updates following the March 2026
Cabinet report, is as follows:
•Completed RIBA Stage 3 design and secured planning permission
(Feb–Apr 2025);
•Undertaken an initial tender exercise, which did not deliver
a viable outcome;
•Reviewed procurement strategy, retaining a two-stage
approach, enabling early contractor involvement to improve cost
certainty and deliverability, and adopted an Open Tender route to
market to boost competition, as referenced in the March Cabinet
Report;
•Completed amendments to the scheme to seek simplification and
savings whilst retaining the overall design concept and layout of
the schemes (February – March 2026);
•Undertaken a second procurement exercise (April–June
2026), receiving strong market interest (10 submissions, 8
compliant);
•Project funding is confirmed within the Council’s
Capital Programme within April 2026 Cabinet Report;
•Completed evaluation and identified a preferred contractor;
and
•Cabinet has approved in principle that the future management
of the housing will be 100% affordable; a future report will be
brought to Cabinet setting out the business case for this
approach.
Legal basis for the decision
The procurement has been undertaken in full compliance with the
Council’s Procurement Procedure Rules and Procurement Act
2023.
A two-stage tender process that was adopted simply means the
contractor can be engaged at an early stage for the purposes of
completion of design and other ancillary services.
The report is therefore, seeking authority to award preconstruction
services contract.
The resultant contract will be sealed.
During the preconstruction services phase, a programme for
demolition or enabling works can be submitted by the contractor and
only if the Council is satisfied, can a decision to award a
contract those works be made. Such a decision will require a
further report.
Also, during the preconstruction services phases, the contractor
will work with the Council’s consultant on the final contract
sum.
Where a contract sum is submitted to the Council by the contractor,
a decision to award such contract, will be subject to further
reports and decision.
It is worth noting that the Council is not bound by the award of
this preconstruction services contract, to award any works
contract.
A suite of contract documents has been prepared for use during the
preconstruction and main works phases.
Next steps
This contract is limited to the PCSA services and does not include
demolition works. As with the Homes for Dovercourt scheme, the PCSA
stage provides a defined period to work collaboratively with the
appointed contractor and wider supply chain to refine the design,
test buildability and progress value engineering, with the aim of
reducing costs and securing a deliverable scheme within the
available funding envelope. This stage will enable proactive risk
management with the appointed contractor to improve cost
certainty.
The tender report identifies a Preferred Bidder and provides:
•A fixed cost of the PCSA stage of £199,184.60;
•An estimate of the Demolition works cost
•An estimate of the main works cost which will be refined
during the PCSA period;
•An estimate of value engineering opportunities on the scheme,
of £215,000 with further savings possible if the
sustainability performance of the design is compromised;
•A programme for completion of the works, with enabling works
commencing on site autumn 2026 including demolition of the car park
within the PCSA period, and agreement of the main build contract
sum in Q4 2026/7.
The tender for the main works contract delivers an estimated
£8.84m in Social Value, including £8.7m spend in local
supply chains, £24,000 spend in reduction of waste through
reuse of products and materials, and £10,000 for in-kind
contributions to local community projects.
The price submitted for the tender return is within the budget of
£18,769,810 allocated to this project in the General Fund
Capital Programme. However, the current estimated main build cost
is currently viewed to allow an insufficient sum for contingency,
at around 3%. Based on best practice and lessons learned from past
projects by the authority, a higher contingency sum is sought.
Value engineering with the contractor during the PCSA stage will
work to achieve this, through refining the design and testing
buildability, with the aim of reducing costs and securing a
deliverable scheme within the available funding envelope.
The programme submitted by the contractor sets out an ambitious
timeline for completion of the works in line with the
Council’s aspirations and funding envelope with the following
key dates:
w/c 20/07/2026: PCSA contract signed
w/c 07/12/2026: Construction commencement
w/c 31/04/2028: Car park structure completed
w/c 08/08/2028: Construction completion
The programme will be subject to detailed review with the
contractor during the PCSA stage, with opportunities sought to
bring forward the completion of the car park and public realm, in
conjunction with liaison with MHCLG as the funder.
Due to programme pressures to have the new car park and residential
block completed within the funding envelope by March 2028, the
preferred contractor’s current programme indicates a need for
the demolition of the car park to take place in tandem with the
PCSA exercise. This timeline will be reviewed with the contractor
and will require a separate decision to be made.
Management of the assets
The site is currently held within the General Fund. In March 2026
Cabinet set out an underlying policy direction and ‘in
principle’ approach for the housing element at Carnarvon
Terrace to be 100% and managed directly by the Council. This is
subject to a future full report to Cabinet, planned for the
milestone of agreeing the final contract sum in Q4 26/7, which will
address considerations of appropriate into the Housing Revenue
Account.
Baily Garner, the Employer's Agent and project’s Quantity
Surveyor has provided a Tender Report on 10/07/2026, with detailed
information about the project and the tender process, with the
basis for recommendation of the preferred contractor.

To authorise implementation of the revised Probationary Procedure
and the associated communication and guidance arrangements
necessary to support its introduction.

(c)    
To keep the implementation and effectiveness of the revised
Probationary Procedure under review as further provisions of the
Employment Rights Act 2025 are brought into force and to make any
consequential amendments required, in accordance with the Director
of People’s delegated authority.

The decision is
made following a review of the Council’s Probationary
Procedure, as detailed in the accompanying report. The revised
procedure is required to ensure the Council’s approach
remains legally compliant, fair and operationally effective in the
light of forthcoming employment legislation, including changes to
unfair dismissal qualifying rights. The revised procedure supports
earlier, structured probation reviews, timely feedback and
decision-making, and appropriate support for employees and
managers.

The option of
retaining the existing six-month probationary period was considered
but rejected for the reasons set out in the accompanying report,
principally because earlier structured review points are required
to ensure fair, supportive timely and legally compliant
decision-making.

purpose:
In November 2016 the Housing Service procured
Chubb Fire and Security Limited to provide Technology Enabled Care
Services (installation, maintenance and repair) in our eight
Sheltered Housing Schemes.
The UK is undergoing a significant transition from analogue phone
lines to digital technologies and the Public Switched Telephone
Network (PSTN) is being retired with the aim of completing the
switch by January 2027. Eight sheltered housing schemes currently
use an analogue telephone line to transfer the digital alarm
service (pull cords, pendants, call box) to the 24/7 call centre
(Amphora/ Helpline).
The Chubb system infrastructure in the effected 253 sheltered
housing dwellings is digital ready, however the main system rack in
each scheme requires work to communicate digitally with the
dedicated Johntec VPN at Amphora/ Helpline. Adding a Chubb room
unit in the annexe block at Belmans Court, Dovercourt has also been
identified as an additional safety measure.
We are committed to providing a 24/7 digital alarm system to our
sheltered housing residents therefore given that the individual
sheltered housing dwellings are digital ready and the significant
risk and cost of moving to an alternative supplier, it is proposed
to use the existing supplier Chubb Fire and Security Ltd within our
existing arrangement covering installation, maintenance and repair
to undertake this work.
Chubb Fire and Security Ltd have provided the following estimated
quotation:
•£3,146.18 + VAT per scheme to supply and fit the
digital set to the system.
•£290.00 + VAT per scheme to supply a SIM on a 1 Year
contract.
•£1,282.67 + VAT to supply an additional Chubb room unit
in the annexe block at Belmans Court.
•TOTAL - £28,772.11 + VAT
We are aware of some market fluctuation in the cost of key digital
components Random Access Memory (RAM) and Solid-State Drive (SSD)
so it is suggested that 5% flexibility of the total cost is allowed
as a contingency.

purpose:
To update the scope of the current Managed
Network Contract with Intergence Systems.
The Council currently have a number of housing schemes across the
District that provide residents with access to an assistance
system. This service connects to the Council through both telephone
lines and broadband, enabling residents to request help when
required. The existing connectivity at these schemes is not
compatible with the new digital telephony and broadband services
being rolled out nationally by BT, and the legacy lines will become
obsolete by the end of this year. As a result, investigative and
remedial works are required to determine what changes are needed at
each scheme.
Similarly, the Council rents a number of telephone lines across our
disparate buildings including: Town Hall, Pier/Barnes House,
leisure centres, Northbourne Depot etc. Again these lines will also
become obsolete reference the above-mentioned BT national roll-out
programme.
The Council has a current Network Managed Contract with Intergence
systems that still has 2 years left and the works required aligns
directly with the contract.
In order for the works to be completed, the scope of the contract
needs to have a minor update that does increase the cost of the
contract by a minimal amount.
With the change in the costs and update of the scope we have gained
clarification from the Council's Contracts, Procurement and
Projects Solicitor who has confirmed that this decision is in
accordance with the Councils Constitution (part 5) and due to the
value of the proposed variation falling below the current threshold
of 10% under regulation 72(5)(b) PCR 2015, the changes are
permitted.
We also have concurrence for the works from the Portfolio Holder
for Environment and IT.
The updated of the scope of the Managed Network Service contract
will offer many benefits, including:
1.Cyber Protection and Support – this will enable us to both
continue and enhance the Security controls and processes we have in
place. Moving to a new supplier will be a prolonged process and may
risk a period of unsupported systems or exposure to poor technical
support knowledge/ capabilities and increase our exposure to cyber
threats. Access to highly secure systems and data associated to our
most vulnerable clients would have to be granted to a new provider,
which would include prolonged checks and agreements, increasing the
amount of time the works would take to complete and thus may
increase the risk considerably of the works not being completed in
the required (BT) national deadline.
2.Value for Money and Business Continuity – continuation of
the managed Network service ensures all the extra services and
monitoring is kept with one supplier thus ensuring value for money,
continuity of service plus a range of ‘value-add’ free
services.
3.Resilience enhancements – The services and the knowledge
and expertise provided by Intergence ensure the Council has a
highly resilient, modern and enabling infrastructure.
4.Single Point of Support – The managed service contract
covers a complex mix of technologies and systems all supported by
one provider. These include Wide Area Network (WAN), Local Area
Network (LAN), Wi-Fi. Therefore, no diffusion of responsibility can
occur.
5.Proven Knowledge and Expertise – working with the said
company for a number of years and on a number of high-level
projects (as previously outlined) has proven Intergence knowledge
and expertise in the field.
6.Security, Governance and Risk – Intergence have Government
level Security clearance (SC) staff at Project, Design and Support
Levels (Security Clearance conforms to BS7858). The company also
has the following Security Governance and Risk Certifications:
ISO:27001, ISO:9001, Cyber Essentials.

content:
To extend the
contract for the Head of Project Delivery Unit (PDU) by a further
60 days covering the period from the start of July to the end of
November 2026, in addition to the current 254 days contracted since
December 2024; and to approve the allocation of a further
£46,020 from the Project Delivery Unit budget to cover the
costs.

Work within the PDU
is ongoing to deliver a suite of capital projects across the
District, alongside partners.
 
In a Decision dated
13/12/2024, approval was given for the allocation of £190,250
to fund the recruitment of a Head of Project Delivery Unit (PDU)
via Talent Bank.
 
The current
postholder’s number of contracted days is due to expire and
therefore consideration has been given to the remaining capital
projects being delivered and the need for a ‘Head of’
role, and the value for money of the position continuing in line
with other PDU staffing resource. The council is currently managing
over £60m of capital delivery expenditure and requires
experienced professional advisors to progress the
works. 
 
It is therefore
proposed to contract a further 60 days of the Head of Unit’s
time, and to allocate the required funding to pay for the costs
from the Project Delivery Unit budget. It should be noted that some
of the post holder’s time can be capitalised against delivery
of individual projects.
 
The ‘Head
of’ role is specifically focused on programme management, and
this decision brings forward the ability to transparently extend
the contract with Talent Bank for uninterrupted work to continue in
line with the original timeline set out for the PDU through to
November 2026.

To not extend the
contract with required funding.
 
The PDU requires
the programme management and capital delivery expertise enabled by
this postholder to manage and continue delivery on the suite of
high value, multi stakeholder capital projects which each has
specific spend criteria and deadlines for use of the allocated
funding via Central Government. To lose this resource would be
detrimental to time-sensitive work and would cause cost to ongoing
projects.
 
To extend beyond 60
days.
 
The PDU as a team
is currently approved for a period of two years from November 2024.
Work is ongoing to review the current position on a wider scale to
ensure continued delivery of projects against value for money. The
future of this ‘Head of’ role beyond November 2026 will
be decided in line with the wider Project Delivery Unit.

decision_maker: Leisure and Public Realm Portfolio Holder
content:
To extend the
householder permit scheme through the months of July and August
2026 for Orwell Place car park, Dovercourt.

Significant public
realm and highway improvement works are currently being undertaken
in Dovercourt, focused on Kingsway and the High Street. While these
works are expected to deliver long-term benefits to the Council, to
the area, they have temporarily reduced the availability of
on-street parking, particularly the existing two-hour free
provision. This has led to concerns from local businesses regarding
reduced accessibility and local a decline in customer footfall.
 
To mitigate these
impacts during the peak summer period, a proposal has been put
forward to provide a form of free parking in Dovercourt throughout
July and August 2026. This would effectively provide an alternative
to the displaced on-street parking and support continued access to
the town centre while works are ongoing.

Option 1 - Do
Nothing; Retain existing parking charges and arrangements.
 
Implication: No
financial impact to the Council but does not address the
significant loss of on-street parking and may further impact town
centre footfall reduced accessibility and businesses during the
works.
 
Option 2 - Remove
Tariffs; (Full Free Parking) Temporarily suspend all parking
charges at Orwell Place car park for July and August 2026
 
Implication:
Provides the strongest mitigation and simplest offer for users;
however, this would result in a direct loss of parking income and
would require either a formal amendment to the parking order or use
of an exemption process to implement within required
timescales.
 
Option 3
Time-Limited Extension of Householder Permit Scheme
 
Preferred
option.
topline: The Leisure and Public Realm Portfolio Holder has decided to extend the householder permit scheme for Orwell Place car park in Dovercourt to address the impact of reduced on-street parking availability during ongoing improvement works.

purpose:
The Council has a statutory duty to ensure
that all electrical installations within its housing stock are
maintained in a safe condition and inspected at appropriate
intervals.
Recent changes in regulatory expectations and the strengthened
consumer regulation regime introduced under the Social Housing
(Regulation) Act 2023 place greater emphasis on proactive
compliance, tenant safety, and demonstrable assurance of landlord
responsibilities. Registered providers are expected to maintain
robust evidence that statutory safety inspections are completed and
that identified risks are remedied within appropriate
timescales.
In addition, the Council must comply with:
•Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector
(England) Regulations 2020, which have become an established
benchmark for electrical safety inspection frequencies.
•Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, requiring landlords to keep
electrical installations in repair and proper working order.
•Housing Act 2004 and the Housing Health and Safety Rating
System (HHSRS), under which electrical hazards are recognised as
potential Category 1 hazards.
•The Regulator of Social Housing Consumer Standards, effective
from April 2024, requiring landlords to meet all applicable
statutory health and safety requirements and manage risks to
tenants appropriately.
The award of this contract will support the Council in maintaining
compliance with the five-year EICR inspection programme and
ensuring that any Category 1 or Category 2 defects identified
during inspections are rectified promptly to maintain resident
safety and minimise regulatory risk.

Service: EICRs Cat 1

purpose:
On 20 December 2024, Cabinet accepted the
Community Regeneration Partnership funding and commenced delivery
of the Ten_09 Jaywick Sands Public Open Spaces project. Subsequent
Cabinet decisions increased the overall project budget and approved
the development of a revised programme of projects.
The original appointment of Adams & Sutherland Ltd was based on
a £1.7m construction budget and a programme of eight public
open space projects. Since appointment, Cabinet-approved changes to
the project budget and scope have significantly increased the scale
and complexity of the programme.
The current programme comprises twelve projects, including
Brooklands Road, Bay Walk, Enterprise Centre and Dig4Jaywick
improvements, vacant plot activation projects and expanded
proposals at Crossways Park and St Christophers Green following
approval of the revised Ten_09 programme and associated budget
increase.
As the project has developed through feasibility, consultation and
design stages, substantially more work has been required including
additional stakeholder engagement, highways and engineering input,
multi-site design development and coordination across a
significantly larger programme of projects.
This decision enables completion of the current design stage and
provides developed proposals to inform future delivery
decisions.

with Section 2 of the Constitution which sub-section 2.1 states: c)

Corporate Director/Head of Department following consultation with

purpose:
Derek Crosfield House is a supported housing
scheme for young people aged 16-25 (single people and couples) who
either have care of a baby or are expecting a child. There are 8
self-contained flats plus communal facilities on site including a
garden, playroom, kitchen and laundry. All the flats are supplied
with a cooker, fridge freezer and carpets
The scheme aims to offer temporary housing and support to young
people whilst they gain confidence as parents and learn the skills
to live independently and manage a permanent tenancy. The length of
stay will depend upon an individual’s needs as will the level
and type of support offered.
Referrals to the service are made by Tendring District Council, in

purpose:
The Council has been providing funding for
rough sleeper early intervention work since 2020. Since June 2020
funding has been awarded to Tendring District Council to help
tackle the problems of rough sleeping found in the Tendring area,
and we have taken unprecedented steps to support rough sleepers.
This work has been undertaken in partnership with Anglia Care Trust
who provide intensive support to clients who are sleeping rough and
help them to find accommodation in the Tendring area, if this is
their home area, or locating back to their home area if it is
outside of the Tendring district.
The support offered also involves engaging with sofa surfers to
prevent them getting into a position whereby they are sleeping
rough.

purpose:

lease.
content:
(1)    
To approve, in principle, the granting of a short
term Licence to Occupy to Clacton Town Football Club Ltd for Rush
Green Bowl;

 

(2)    
To note that an open tender process will be
undertaken to secure a longer term lease;
 

(3)    
To approve the terms for a short-term licence to Clacton Town
Football Club Ltd on the proposed terms and conditions; and
 

(4)    
To authorise the Corporate Director (Planning and Community) to
complete the licence on the agreed terms and on such any other
terms as he considers appropriate.

To
regularise current occupation arrangements and ensure appropriate
legal and governance controls.  As well
as enabling continued community use of the facility whilst allowing
time for a compliant and transparent tender process.
 

Option 1: Require
immediate vacant possession of the site - this would disrupt the
current community benefit of the site and mean the current football
club operating from the site will lose their place in the league,
prejudicing their position when it comes to submitting a
tender.
 
Option 2: Immediate
grant of a lease – the Council has had numerous expressions
of interest, and this would not allow market testing and could
expose the Council to challenge.
 
Option 3: Do
nothing – this would leave the current occupation unregulated
and present legal and operational risks, and the current
third-party occupier has been engaging in a positive manner who are
also keen to regularise the occupation.

content:
To report back to
the Portfolio Holder for Assets and Community Safety the responses
so far received from Harwich Town Council, Frinton & Walton
Town Council and Brightlingsea Town Council in respect of their
interest in potential Community Asset Transfer. This follows the
establishment of a provisional programme of work in January 2026
and formally writing to those Councils seeking their confirmation
of participation and feedback on the programme.
 
The report then
sets out recommendations for progressing relevant discussions,
amending the work programme accordingly and putting resources in
place to oversee the necessary work.


a)    to note the contents of
the supporting report and to agree the revised Programme of Work in
respect of pre-LGR Community Asset Transfer set out within that
report, having received a formal expression of interest from
Brightlingsea Town Council and a less advanced confirmation of
participation from Harwich Town Council and Frinton & Walton
Town Council;

 

b)    to agree that the focus
of the Programme of Work will be to progress the potential transfer
of assets to Brightlingsea Town Council, having received its formal
expression of interest and to progress the potential transfer of
the Columbine Centre in Walton on the Naze to Frinton & Walton Town Council, and to
instruct the Corporate Director (Planning and Community) to proceed
with the implementation of this programme;

 

c)    to agree that
discussions and the sharing of information related to the potential
for the transfer of other assets to Harwich Town Council and
Frinton & Walton Town Council can continue, but in line with
the Council’s normal approach under its Community Asset
Transfer Policy, and not necessarily ahead of LGR and not as part
of the defined Programme of Work to be supported by a dedicated
resource;  

 

d)    to note and agree that
resource implications will be revisited once there is a clearer
indication of costs and that decisions on the budget for appointing
external expertise in respect of valuation, business case
development/analysis and legal support will be taken by the Cabinet
in due course, as would any subsequent decision about the transfer
of specific assets; and

 

e)    to note that Officers
are still in the process of administering the Property Dealing
Procedure in respect of the potential transfer of the Columbine
Centre to Frinton & Walton Town Council having issued draft
Heads of Terms in March 2026, with the aim of any such transfer
being completed by November 2026.

To revise the
previously-agreed Programme of Work in respect of pre-LGR Community
Asset Transfer and confirm the focus of work having received a
clear expression of interest from Brightlingsea Town Council and
feedback from Harwich Town Council and Frinton & Walton Town
Council indicating an interest in continued discussion about the
potential transfer of assets, but without a firm proposal at this
stage as to what assets to include in the scope.


(1)    
To continue discussions on an informal basis; or

 

(2)    
To abandon the idea of a managed process of exploring the transfer
of groups of assets to Brightlingsea Town Council or others, and
simply leave those bodies to come forward with proposals to obtain
individual assets or groups of assets, which can be considered
against the Council’s current Community Asset Transfer policy
and property dealing procedures in the normal, as opposed to a
collaborative, way; or

 

(3)    
To build more time into the programme for Harwich Town Council and
Frinton & Walton Town Council to develop a clear expression of
interest, and for the programme to be adjusted accordingly for all
three Councils’ propositions to be assessed and considered at
the same time, as originally envisaged.

decision_maker: Corporate Director (Place & Wellbeing) & Deputy Chief Executive
purpose:
The Milton Road and Victoria Street schemes
form part
of the Council’s Local Regeneration Fund programme,
which will deliver regeneration of two sites, including a
refurbished public car park and 8 new affordable
homes.
A competitive procurement exercise has been
undertaken, identifying a preferred bidder following
strong market interest and evaluation of submissions.
The appointment of the contractor under a PCSA will
enable early contractor involvement to:
• refine the detailed design;
• identify and manage risks; and
• develop a robust and deliverable contract sum
for the main works.
This stage is critical to progressing the scheme within
the required programme and funding timescales,
including the requirement to expend funding by March
2028.
This decision relates to the initial PCSA stage. At the
conclusion of this stage, the contractor will develop and
submit a final contract sum for the main construction
works, which will be subject to a further officer decision
(in consultation with Portfolio Holders) prior to entering
into a main works contract.

purpose:
On 6 October 2023 Cabinet considered a report
titled ‘Levelling Up Fund and Capital Regeneration Projects -
Progressing the Projects to Planning Permission’. As part of
that report, Cabinet delegated authority to the Corporate Director
Place and Economy in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism to procure appropriate
resources and commission a project team to carry out the associated
work including for the design briefs.
UKPN have an existing substation to the rear of the development
site, with a right of way to allow them vehicular access across the
site to the substation including for maintenance.
At present the right of way provides unrestricted access across the
site, which requires a Deed of Variation to restrict the wayleave
in response to the development proposals and planning consent for
the redevelopment of the site.
The proposed variation provides UKPN with a 3m wide vehicular route
and has secured their agreement.

decision_maker: Corporate Director (Place & Wellbeing) & Deputy Chief Executive
purpose:
This decision builds on the previously
approved
Brooklands Road temporary repairs (Officer’s Decision),
and forms part of the wider Ten_09 Jaywick Public
Open Spaces project, approved by Cabinet (March
2025) and Portfolio Holder (August 2025).
Intrusive site investigations are required, as
recommended by the appointed civil engineers, to
inform an assessment of options and potential future
design for any road upgrade, specifically to:
• confirm road construction and ground conditions;
and
• identify and assess the condition of existing toe
drain infrastructure.
This information is critical to informing a future decision
on whether to proceed with upgrading Brooklands Road
and to reducing risk associated with unknown ground
conditions, including cost management.
Alternative Site Investigation quotes were obtained via
the project consultant team and in line with the
Council’s
Quotation Rules; however, these identified the works as
more appropriate for a highways/civils contractor and
costs indicated were comparatively high.
Groupbridge Ltd are mobilised on site delivering the
approved temporary works, and allow the undertaking of
the investigations concurrently which:
• minimises additional mobilisation and traffic
management costs;
• reduces disruption to residents; and
• represents the most efficient and cost-effective
delivery approach.
This decision does not commit the Council to
undertaking any road upgrade works and is solely to
gather evidence to inform a future decision.

purpose:
This decision forms part of the wider Milton
Road and Victoria Street schemes, approved by Cabinet as part of
the Local Regeneration Fund programme.
Additional intrusive ground investigations are required to support
the Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) stage and to inform
detailed design development, particularly in relation to foundation

buildability and enable a more robust scheme with greater cost
certainty.
It has not been possible to carry out this investigation previously
as demolition of the derelict building was awaited.

purpose:
Hesselberg Erosion Protection are the original
installers of the Open Stone Asphalt system at these locations and
have specialist expertise in both its construction and
repair.
They appear to be the only contractor currently offering this
specialist OSA repair service, including the specific materials,
techniques and knowledge required to carry out the works
effectively.
Due to the specialist nature of the product and repair methodology,
it is considered that:
- There is no viable alternative provider capable of delivering
equivalent works
- Competitive procurement would not provide meaningful
competition
- Delaying works to undertake a full procurement process would
increase the risk of further deterioration and associated
costs.
In addition, the condition at West End Lane has worsened since the
initial surveys, with large sections now missing. This increases
the urgency of the works and strengthens the need for immediate
appointment of a suitably qualified contractor.
Failure to act promptly may result in:
- Significant damage to coastal defence infrastructure
- Increased repair costs
- Potential risk to the adjacent landfill site
- Greater disruption and more extensive works in future

decision_maker: Corporate Director (Place & Wellbeing) & Deputy Chief Executive
purpose:
In April 2026 Cabinet approved funding in the
value of £42,000.00 for the extension of the district wide
business support for 2026 – 2027.
A Request for Quotation (RFQ) was completed in line with current
procurement rules and regulations. Four business support companies
were invited to respond; two submitted completed quotations, while
two declined to participate.
A scoring panel was established to assess the two submissions. To
ensure impartiality, the panel was independent of the Economic
Growth team. Each panel member evaluated the quotations separately
and independently. A moderation meeting was then held to review and
consolidate scores, and to agree the final scoring.
Following this process, Colbea achieved the highest score of the
two quotations received.

decision_maker: Corporate Director (Place & Wellbeing) & Deputy Chief Executive
purpose:
Since its announcement on 1 October 2023 by
the UK Government at the time, Clacton-on-Sea has been part of a
programme in which a Town Board would be formed from local
community, service and business representatives, it would develop a
10 year Vision for the Town and then receive a total of £20M
of funding to deliver that Vision. To support the development of
the Vision and achieve some quick wins, the UK Government has
supported the programme with (what is now) a total of £600K
'capacity' funding.
In July 2025 (Minute 44 refers), in considering the appropriate
arrangements for the allocation and approval of Pride in Place
Capacity funding, Cabinet approved that "the Corporate Director
(Place and Wellbeing) be authorised to approve variations of the
[...] capacity payments, upon receipt of minuted approval by the
Clacton Town Board, and following consultation with the
Council’s Section 151 Officer."
The Clacton Town Board on 30 March 2026 was advised that the UK
Government had endorsed its 10 Year Vision (submitted in late 2025)
and, following some clarifications, the Year 1 delivery funding
would be provided to the Council as the Accountable Body for the
Clacton programme). In view of this, and the final element of the
overall £600K capacity funding, the Board reallocated its
capacity funding and determined in part its use of the Year 1
delivery funding to be provided.
The minuted decision of the Clacton Town Board in respect of
reallocation of capacity funding has been provided to the Corporate
Director (Place and Wellbeing). The Section 151 Officer has also
been consulted. The Board's decision
On 24 April 2026 (Minute 141 refers), the Council's Cabinet
approved:
"Pride In Place external grant funding of £0.360m (capital)
and £0.232m (revenue), along with associated additional
capacity funding of £0.150m to support the delivery of the
programme, be accepted ahead of a future separate report that will
include further details / associated governance arrangements as
necessary."

decision_maker: Leader of the Council and Corporate Finance & Governance Portfolio Holder
content:
To approve Freeport
East’s Business Plan 2026/27, which was presented at the
Freeport East Supervisory Board on 2 February 2026.

The Board approved the
draft Business Plan for 2026/27 for submission to Members for their
approval. Both Cllr. Ivan Henderson, Deputy Leader of the Council
and Lee Heley, Deputy Chief Executive of the Council supported the
adoption of the plan.
In order to adopt the
plan, a written board resolution is required as under the
Freeport’s Government approved governance arrangements
(including the Memorandum of Understanding and Full Business Case),
key strategic and financial documents must be explicitly approved
by the Board and recorded in writing to provide a clear audit trail
and assurance to government, the Accountable Body, and partner
councils.
The written resolution
confirms that the Board has properly agreed the plan, ensures
spending and delivery activity are lawfully authorised, supports
local authority audit and accountability requirements, and protects
board members by clearly evidencing the decision.

purpose:
This report records the
officer decision to renew the Council’s contract for the
Oneserve housing repairs system for a further two-year period from
14 May 2026 to 13 May 2028. Oneserve is the Council’s
end-to-end operational system for managing housing repairs and
associated works and is integral to the delivery of statutory
housing services, providing the core workflow for job creation,
scheduling, engineer allocation, progress tracking, cost control
and performance reporting. The existing contract expired in January
2026, and continued use of the system is necessary to maintain
uninterrupted operational delivery. The renewal has been structured
as a dual-contract arrangement, with the majority of the services
procured via the G-Cloud Framework and a parallel contract
maintained outside the framework to cover essential non-standard
system requirements that are not available through G-Cloud. The
decision reflects that the system is proprietary and can only be
supplied, licenced, supported and maintained by the incumbent
provider, making a competitive procurement exercise unviable.
Renewal represents the lowest-risk and most economically
advantageous option when compared to re-procurement or system
replacement, which would introduce significant cost, data
migration, operational and service continuity risks, particularly
in the context of Local Government Reorganisation. Concurrence to
the exemption from the Procurement Procedure Rules and the renewal
of the contract was obtained from Damian Williams, Corporate
Director (Operations & Delivery); Richard Barrett, Corporate
Director (Finance & IT); Councillor Andy Baker, (Portfolio
Holder for Housing & Planning); and Councillor M. Stephenson,
(Leader of the Council and Corporate Finance & Governance
Portfolio Holder).

purpose:
The Council is undertaking a review of Gypsy
and Traveller accommodation need as part of its Local Plan work.
The most recent Gypsy and Traveller Accommodation Assessment (GTAA)
(December 2024) identified a level of need that requires further
deliverability work to inform the Council’s evidence base and
policy approach.
Commissioning a Pitch Deliverability Assessment (PDA) will provide
robust advice on whether, and to what extent, identified needs
could be met through the intensification, reconfiguration or
expansion of existing sites in the District. The PDA will apply the
deliverability tests set out in national policy and will include
desk based review and engagement with site owners/managers and
residents, producing clear findings capable of withstanding
scrutiny.
ORS has specialist expertise in Gypsy and Traveller needs
assessments and deliverability work and has experience of producing
PDAs for other local authorities. Procuring ORS will enable the
Council to obtain a comprehensive, consistent and objective
assessment within required timescales, supporting Local Plan
preparation and related decision making.
The fixed fee of £6,955 + VAT represents a proportionate cost
for a defined programme of work, including post project advice. The
outputs (summary report and completed site matrices) will directly
support the Council’s statutory plan making responsibilities
and provide value for money compared with undertaking the work in
house or commissioning multiple separate inputs.
content:
To approve:
1. The procurement and
award of a contract to Opinion Research Services (ORS) to undertake
a Gypsy and Traveller Pitch Deliverability Assessment (PDA) to
support the Council’s Local Plan evidence base; and
2. Acceptance of
ORS’s proposal (April 2026) and fee for delivery of the PDA,
including post project advice as set out in the proposal.
The PDA will provide the
Council with robust evidence on the availability, suitability and
achievability of existing Gypsy and Traveller sites to help meet
identified pitch needs and will be used to inform emerging Local
Plan policy, site deliverability work and decision making.

purpose:
The Government has consulted on proposals to
reform arrangements for planning decisions and to introduce a
national scheme of delegation that will make it law for the vast
majority of applications to be determined by Officers, and not
Planning Committees – with strict criteria for applications
are exceptionally referred to Committee.
https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/planning-committee-reform-draft-regulations-and-guidance/planning-committee-reform-statutory-consultation-on-draft-regulations-and-guidance

The Government intends for the changes to come into force from 30th
September 2026.
The changes will mean that all minor residential and commercial
planning applications have to be determined by Officers as well as
all reserved matters applications (unless they relate to phased
developments). When it comes to major outline or full applications,
and reserved matters applications on phased developments, the
judgement as to whether they go to Committee will lie with a
nominated Member and a nominated Officer – normally the
Chairman of Planning Committee and the Chief Planning Officer. Even
applications by the Council, on Council land or put forward by
Council Members or Officers will only go to Committee if the
Chairman of Planning Committee and Chief Planning Officer agree to
it.
Where the Chairman and the Chief Planning Officer do not agree, it
is the Officer’s judgement which prevails.
Councils will not be allowed to have Member call-in arrangements
anymore.
The response, which has been drafted and submitted in consultation
with the Portfolio Holder responsible for Housing and Planning and
the Chairman of the Planning Committee, raises concern that the
proposals are disproportionate, undemocratic and could have
unintended consequences in undermining public confidence in the
planning system and the important role of democratically elected
Councillors in decision making on locally important and sometimes
contentious planning proposals.

content:
a)      
To approve the use of up to £60,000 of Public Health funding
to commission a series of pilot projects called Active Wellbeing
Pilots;
 

b)      
To approve the Active Wellbeing criteria; and
 

c)      
To authorise the Head of Sport & Leisure and the Head of Health
& Community, in consultation with the relevant Portfolio
Holders, to approve the allocation of funding for services.

The Active
Wellbeing pilot projects will be commissioned as part of the new
Active Wellbeing Fund which will support projects that deliver
outcomes across the shared objectives of Sport & Leisure and
Health & Community.
 
The Health and
Wellbeing Strategy (Decision
- Report of the Portfolio Holder for Partnerships - A.5 - Adoption
of a Health & Wellbeing Strategy for Tendring) and
Sport and Activity Strategy (Decision
- Cabinet Members' Items - Report of the Leisure and Public Realm
Portfolio Holder - A.6 - Sport and Activity Strategy for
Tendring) are closely aligned; both strategies aim to
support healthy lifestyles and address wider determinants of health
through physical activity. Developing a joint approach enables the
benefits of both strategies to be amplified simultaneously with a
breadth of outreach, scale and impact.
 
The strategic
budgets allocated aim to address five themes (Women & Girls,
Social Isolation Amongst Older People, Children & Families,
Rehabilitation for Long Term Health Conditions and Arts &
Culture). This underpins the overlapping strategic aims that
address health inequalities amongst targeted demographics and
commission sustainable community development programmes.
 
The proposed Active
Wellbeing pilot projects enable progress to be made rapidly on the
Active Wellbeing Fund with a key consideration of localising
community projects and services for towns across Tendring.

To not align
funding across Sport & Leisure and Health & Community to
address shared priorities in our district through the delivery of
five pilot projects. However, there are strong synergies between
health, wellbeing, and sport and activity and the council’s
strategic approach to both issues. A joint fund provides the
opportunity to deliver benefits for active wellbeing. By not
delivering pilot projects first, there would be no opportunity for
a period of testing and learning before the longer-term Active
Wellbeing Fund services are launched, ensuring the services are
designed with the right focus.
topline: The Leisure and Public Realm Portfolio Holder has decided to approve the use of Public Health funding for Active Wellbeing pilot projects.

purpose:
Tendring District Council is required to
undertake statutory public consultations on Local Plan documents
under the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and associated
Regulations. These consultations routinely generate a large volume
of representations that must be read, analysed and summarised to
inform consultation reporting and subsequent stages of plan
making.
The introduction of PlanAI provides an opportunity to improve the
efficiency, consistency and robustness of this process by
supporting officers with the analysis and summarisation of
consultation responses. The tool operates on pseudonymised data
extracted from the Council’s existing JDi Opus Consult system
and is designed to identify key themes, produce consistent
summaries and support more transparent evidence based
reporting.
Advice has been received from the Council’s Data Protection
Officer and corporate cyber team, both of whom have confirmed that
the risks associated with the use of PlanAI have been appropriately
assessed and mitigated through the completion of a full Data
Protection Impact Assessment and cyber security review. The DPIA
confirms that the residual risk to data subjects is low and
acceptable.
The PlanAI tool has been designed to integrate directly with the
Council’s existing JDi Opus Consult system and has been
validated through use with other local authorities. Procuring
PlanAI provides best value for money compared to alternative
approaches, avoids duplication of systems, and enhances the
Council’s existing consultation infrastructure rather than
replacing it.
PlanAI will be used solely as an officer-support tool to identify
key themes, trends and summaries within consultation responses. All
outputs generated by PlanAI will be reviewed and validated by
Planning Officers, and all decision making will remain with Council
Officers and elected Members.

content:
To fund 43
projects, as listed in the Background Letter, with Sport &
Activity 2024-28 allocation of £29,600 from the Sport and
Activity Strategy Budget.

The Leader of the
Council / Cabinet Member for Corporate Finance & Governance is
approving the highest scoring funding applications as recommended
by the scoring panel.
 
On 11th December
2025, Cabinet Members approved a £23,400 allocation of funds
from the Sport and Activity Strategy towards the first year of
strategic funding (Decision - Allocation of funds from the Sport
and Activity Strategy budget).
 
Following a series
of Sports Forums which took place at the start of 2026 (January and
February), an approved surplus of £6,200 (Decision - Sport
Strategy Funding 2026 Grants), as a result
of positive outreach and community engagement was issued to
ensure all high scoring applications that met the required pass
mark could be funded.
 
The first year of
Sport Strategy Funding made available for 2026 has allocated a
total budget of £29,600 of strategic funds to activate
Tendring’s local community groups under priority areas,
identified within the Sport & Activity Strategy for locally led
delivery.
 
Prior to the
submission, applicants must acknowledge a declaration to adhere to
the requirements of the fund and all monitoring and impact
responsibilities.
 
A scoring panel of
officers drawn from across the council and sport/physical activity
organisations assessed the funding applications to identify
successful submissions.  The
applications were cross-referenced to the grant criteria and
required pass mark before being awarded funding up to £350,
£500, £700 or £1000 in exceptional
circumstances.
 
The grant funding
opportunities were categorised from strategic consultation with
locally based sport and activity delegate groups and are as
follows: 
 

•    To fund the
Workforce and Coach Education grant (£8,140);

•    To fund the Actives
Spaces & Places grant (£17,873.18); and

•    To fund the Active
Travel grant (£3,586.82).
 

Not to allocate
funding and thereby reducing opportunities for local organisations
to activate communities with sport and physical activity
schemes. 
 
To give the funding
to alternative projects, however the proposed applications have
been selected by the scoring panel.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve the allocation of £29,600 from the Sport and Activity Strategy Budget to fund 43 projects.

purpose:
The CCS confirms that the VAS Framework
(RM6259) supports award through the digital catalogue on the
Government eMarketplace, a route already validated through multiple
public sector award decisions.
An award under VAS is permissible as IDOX meets all relevant
framework requirements, specifically:
•Accredited and pre approved supplier:IDOX is fully accredited
and pre approved on the VAS (RM6259) framework, having completed
all CCS vetting and public sector procurement capability
checks.
•IDOX is an authorised supplier under Lot 3: Housing,
Environmental and Planning Solutions, covering planning, building
control, environmental health, licensing, land charges and related
regulatory services.
•Solution alignment: The required products and services
directly align with solutions Idox is authorised to supply under
VAS, meeting the framework’s requirement that the
buyer’s needs are satisfied by catalogue listed
offerings.
•Catalogue listed and established solutions:
IDOX provides well established, standardised software modules that
are listed within the digital catalogue, making them suitable for
award without the need for further competition.
•Framework compliant procurement:
IDOX’s inclusion on the framework ensures that all mandatory
CCS procurement, accreditation, and performance standards are met,
providing a fully compliant and low risk procurement route.
The IDOX suite of products included within this contract provides
the Council with a suite of business critical property-based
systems. The systems are used daily to support a wide range of
functions, including Planning, Building Control, Estate Management,
Environmental Health, Anti Social Behaviour, Private Sector
Housing, Licensing, the Gazetteer, and Local Land Charges.
The value of the contract over the three-year term is as
follows:
Year 1 = £182,366.69
Year 2 = £191,485.02
Year 3 = £201,059.27
Total contract cost £574,910.98
The first-year costs can be met from within existing budgets as an
associated cost pressure was included as part of the budget setting
process for 2026/27.
Costs for subsequent years will be managed within departmental
budgets.
The following benefits will be accrued.
1)A trusted technology support partner. IDOX has established a
strong reputation for technical expertise in the market and
continues to maintain excellent relationships with Tendring
District Council.
IDOX have a presence in all the Essex LAs, specifically Uniform
Planning, Local Land Charges and Public Access, which is used in
every Essex LA except Epping Forest and Colchester, although
Colchester have just signed a 3-year agreement with IDOX to
implement Uniform Planning and Building Control.
2)Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) In light of the recent
announcement, it is worth noting that Braintree has held a long
standing contract with IDOX, while Colchester have recently signed
a 3-year agreement and are in the process of migrating to IDOX from
an alternative supplier.
3)Cybersecurity and Information Governance. IDOX hold the following
Security Governance and Risk Certifications: ISO:27001, ISO:9001,
ISO45001, ISO14001, ISO22301, ISMS0001, ISMS0001, ISMS0005,
ISMS0029, ISO27001 and Cyber Essentials.
4)Value for Money. The fees and charges outlined above are
comparable with current IT industry market rates. In addition, the
prices quoted are in line with IDOX’s CPI uplift of 5%, which
represents a fair and consistent annual adjustment.
5)Partner ethos. Neighbouring authorities also use the same
solution and are willing to work alongside council IT resources to
share knowledge/ information, assisting in the development of new
skills sets, to improve the current system and implement new
processes to benefit both the organisation and the residents of
Tendring.
6)Software and application expertise. Within the public service
sector there are a relatively small number of niche information
technology service providers and very few that cater for all the
above council needs in one complete application.
7)Cost of Change and Business Continuity. Changing the current
solution would cause significant disruption for Tendring residents
during the transition to an alternative system, given the
Council’s critical reliance on the existing platform. Any
change would also require dual running of systems, resulting in
increased operational costs.
Furthermore, it is worth noting that implementing and migrating to
a new system of this complexity would take approximately
12–18 months to plan and deliver. Such a transition would
incur substantial costs, including staff retraining and the
additional resources required to support and complete the
migration.
8)Framework agreement procurement In accordance with the
Council’s procurement rules, this contract renewal will be
undertaken through the Crown Commercial Service (CCS) Vertical
Application Solutions (VAS) Framework (RM6259).
9)Funded using existing budgets. The first-year costs can be met
from within existing budgets as an associated cost pressure was
included as part of the budget setting process for 2026/27.

content:
To allocate
£3,000 from the Public Health budget to support the running
of the 2026 Younger Persons Crucial Crew.
 

The Community
Safety Team are seeking to run Younger Person’s Crucial Crew
events in 2026, building on successful events in 2025.  The cost of running the events is £10,000
and £7,000 has already been secured and there is a request
for the remaining £3,000.  Crucial
Crew will support young people to make good choices and develop
resilience and opportunity as they are informed at the Crucial Crew
events around public health issues such as knife crime, young
person’s situational awareness and safety, dangers to look
out for, gang awareness and emergency planning.  This meets the priority in the Council’s
Health and Wellbeing Strategy in relation to improving wellbeing
and resilience as it seeks to empower young people to make the
right choices which will support their mental health and future
opportunity.  It will also support them
to be able to engage in a healthier lifestyle by being better
informed.
 
Link to the Council’s
Health and Wellbeing Strategy:
 

Microsoft Word - A.5 Report - Health
and Wellbeing Strategy
 

Tendring Health & Wellbeing
Strategy Lv
 
 
 

To not fund the
project and use the funding for a different public health
intervention.
 
Although there is
demand for allocating funding to public health work the Younger
Persons Crucial Crew is tried and tested and has delivered strong
outcomes in terms of support for young people to make good choices
which supports their future opportunity.
